---
title: localmap
---

`localmap` creates reproducible maps, site-attribute tables, and provenance for
configured Tasmanian field sites. Start with one of two deliberately separate
routes.

## Deterministic JC demonstration

```sh
make bootstrap
LOCALMAP_ALLOW_NETWORK=0 LOCALMAP_ALLOW_LARGE_DOWNLOADS=0 R_CONFIG_ACTIVE=jc_ci TARGETS_PROFILE=ci make pipeline
```

`jc_ci` uses packaged occurrence and camera-site fixtures, offline WMS/ArcGIS
placeholders, and disabled topographic tiles. It does not promise
`outputs/jc/maps/species_topo.png`; placeholder layers are not live imagery.

## Real-data settings route

`settings.example.yaml` is a real-data-only template. Before running it,
`site.csv` must exist in the configured input directory with `site`, `lat`, and
`lon` columns. `obs.csv` and `op.csv` are optional. These input files are not
included in the checkout.

After `make bootstrap`, run the source-loading checkout wrapper:

```sh
Rscript scripts/run_project.R settings.example.yaml
```

If `localmap` has instead been installed as an R package, use its public API:

```r
localmap::run_settings("settings.example.yaml")
```

Read the [settings guide](settings.md) for inputs and field resolution, then use
the [pipeline overview](PIPELINE.md), [configuration reference](config_reference.md),
[layer guide](layers_guide.md), and [output guide](output_schema_v1.md) as needed.

Package-level examples are in the
[getting-started vignette](../pkgdown/articles/intro.html), all public functions
are in the [reference index](../pkgdown/reference/index.html), and the rendered
fixture-backed evidence is in the [JC report](../reports/paper.html).
